exact.эмалированная кружка со сколом: an enamel mug with a chip
exact.Вот кружка, эмаль на боку отбита. Я из н: Here's the mug, the enamel's knocked off the side. I drank tea out of it for so many years that the chip looks like a pattern now.
exact.В Пекине перемены входили через улицу: с: In Beijing changes came in through the street: first the tram, then the metro and wide roads where the walls used to stand. And one day the neighbours started gathering at whoever got a television first.
exact.Как-то зимой я пошла за капустой и верну: One winter I went out for cabbage and came back with two string bags, because the woman at the stall said there'd be none tomorrow. Next day there was cabbage, and we ate ours till spring, laughing, and couldn't look at it any more.
exact.открытка с рекой Хуанпу: a postcard of the Huangpu River
exact.Это открытка с Хуанпу, на обороте ничего: This is a postcard of the Huangpu, there's nothing written on the back. I bought it to send to someone and never decided who.
exact.В Шанхае перемены были слышны: гудок вер: In Shanghai you could hear the changes: the shipyard hooter, the tram bell, then bridges over the Huangpu and the metro. Mum used to say the city changed faster than she could learn the new stops.
exact.Однажды мы с подругой решили сварить пел: Once my friend and I decided to make dumplings for the whole flat and mixed enough dough for the whole street. The neighbours came round with their own bowls, and we pretended we'd planned it that way.
exact.квитанция из велосипедной мастерской: a receipt from a bicycle repair shop
exact.Вот квитанция из велосипедной мастерской: Here's a receipt from the bicycle repair shop, the ink's almost faded. The bicycle's long gone, and for some reason I keep the slip.
exact.В Гуанчжоу перемены приходили по реке и: In Guangzhou changes came by river and by rail: new bridges, the station, the fair that brought in strangers. At home people talked about them as if the city moved house a little each time.
exact.Как-то летом пошёл такой ливень, что мы: One summer it poured so hard that the neighbour and I sat under a shop awning all evening. In the end the owner brought us a stool and some tea each, and the rain still didn't stop.
exact.фарфоровая чашка с крышкой: a porcelain cup with a lid
exact.Видишь, чашка с крышкой, а блюдца нет. Б: See, a cup with a lid, and no saucer. The saucer broke ages ago, and the lid, oddly enough, is still in one piece.
exact.В Чэнду перемены приезжали вместе с людь: In Chengdu changes arrived along with people: institutes from other cities, then factories, then new districts on the edge of town. Mum kept saying the city had got crowded, and then she got used to it.
exact.Однажды я сварила такой острый суп, что: Once I made a soup so hot that my brother drank water straight from the kettle. He sulked, and the next day he asked for more, just so long as nobody saw.
exact.открытка с мостом через Янцзы: a postcard of the bridge over the Yangtze
exact.Это открытка с мостом через Янцзы. Я её: This is a postcard of the bridge over the Yangtze. I keep it in a book, and the book falls open at that page by itself now.
exact.В Ухане всё решала река: мост, паводки,: In Wuhan the river decided everything: the bridge, the floods, the steelworks. When the water rose, every table talked about it, and when the bridge opened, people went to look at it as if they were paying a visit.
exact.Летом было так жарко, что мы выносили кр: One summer it was so hot that we carried the beds outside and slept right there, the whole courtyard. At night somebody always started telling scary stories, and then nobody could sleep at all.
exact.будильник, который отстаёт на минуту: an alarm clock that runs a minute slow
exact.Вот будильник, он отстаёт ровно на минут: Here's the alarm clock, it runs exactly a minute slow. I never set it right, I got used to living a minute behind.
exact.В Сиани перемены всё время выкапывали из: In Xi'an changes kept being dug out of the ground or brought from far away: a university from Shanghai, then a find people later came from far away to see. There seems to be more lying under the city than standing on it.
exact.Однажды мы с сестрой полдня лепили лапшу: Once my sister and I spent half a day making noodles and fell out over whose were thicker. Dad ate both bowls and said he couldn't tell the difference, and we were both cross with him.
exact.ключ от комнаты, которой больше нет: the key to a room that's no longer there
exact.Это ключ от нашей старой комнаты. Дома д: This is the key to our old room. The house is long gone, there's something else in its place, and I never threw the key away.
exact.Шэньчжэнь сначала был рыночным посёлком: Shenzhen was a market town by the railway at first, and then within a few years it became a city I didn't recognise. At home we kept arguing whether to be glad of it or to hold on to the old.
exact.Как-то мы с соседкой пошли на рынок за р: Once the neighbour and I went to the market for fish, got talking, and bought one between the two of us. Then we spent ages deciding who got the head and who got the tail, and in the end we made soup together.
exact.щепотка соли в бумажном свёртке: a pinch of salt in a paper twist
exact.Вот, в бумажке соль, совсем немного. Я е: Here, there's salt in this paper, just a little. I don't keep it for eating, just to have it.
exact.В Цзыгуне всё начиналось с соли: скважин: In Zigong everything started with salt: the wells, then the works, and then the lanterns and the dinosaur bones people came to see. Mum was surprised that people far away suddenly knew about our town.
exact.Однажды тётя пересолила рыбу так, что её: Once my aunt oversalted the fish so badly it had to be soaked in three changes of water. My uncle said that's the only way they know how in Zigong, and my aunt didn't speak to him till evening.
exact.тетрадка с записью трудодней: an exercise book with work points in it
exact.Вот тетрадка, тут трудодни записаны, кар: Here's the exercise book, the work points are written in pencil, you can barely see them. It's not my handwriting, and yet somehow I'm the one who kept it.
exact.В Гуанхане перемены начинались с поля: к: In Guanghan changes started in the fields: how to divide the land, who's responsible for what, what our township's called. And then training planes began flying over us, and it was years before the children stopped craning their necks.
exact.Как-то весной сосед купил утят, а они уш: One spring a neighbour bought some ducklings, and they followed me out to the field and wouldn't leave me all day. In the evening he came to fetch them and took a long time to believe I hadn't lured them away.
This is a grain sack, patched all over. I keep scraps of cloth in it now, and I can't bring myself to throw it out.
exact.В Сяогане всё решала земля: сколько с не: In Xiaogang the land decided everything: how much it would yield and who it belonged to. When that changed, the village was silent for a long time at first, and then talked of nothing else.
exact.Однажды на свадьбе у соседей я так разош: Once at the neighbours' wedding I got so carried away that I sang louder than anyone, though I didn't know the words. For a year afterwards they kept asking me to sing, and every time I said no and sang anyway.
exact.Я с детства работала в поле вместе со вс: I'd worked in the fields since I was little, along with everyone in the house, and when I grew up it simply became my job. Nobody asked whether I wanted to, they asked whether it had come up.
exact.Поле было то же, менялось только, кто сч: The field was the same, the only thing that changed was who counted the harvest and how it was shared. I learnt to tell rain from the sky, and I was wrong less often than the neighbour who boasted about it.
exact.От поля я отошла, когда спина перестала: I left the fields when my back stopped doing what it was told. And in spring I still wake before everyone else and don't know why.
exact.Я пошла работать в поле вместе со всеми,: I went to work in the fields with everyone else, for work points. In the evening the recorder wrote down how many each of us had, and people argued about that more often than about the weather.
exact.К тому времени я знала, сколько трудодне: By then I knew how many work points every job was worth and could have done the recorder's sums for him. They didn't come to much money, so we thought more about grain than about yuan.
exact.От поля я отошла, когда стало тяжело. А: I left the fields when it got too hard. And when the land was shared out among households again, I'd walk past other people's plots and weed them in my head.
exact.Меня поставили учётчицей, потому что я у: They made me the recorder because I could write numbers neatly. In the evening people came to me with questions, and I soon realised neat numbers don't make everyone happy.
exact.Я наизусть знала, кто сколько заработал: I knew by heart who'd earned how much in a year, and I never told anyone. That was harder than the counting.
exact.Когда землю раздали по дворам, считать т: When the land was shared out among households, there was no one left to count work points for and no reason to, and I went back to the fields. I didn't throw my exercise books away for a long time.
exact.После учительских курсов меня отправили: After the teacher-training course they sent me to a village school. There were more pupils than benches, and half of them only came when there was no work in the fields.
exact.Я учила уже младших братьев и сестёр сво: I was already teaching the younger brothers and sisters of my first pupils. They wrote their characters as if they were ploughing, deep and crooked.
exact.Из школы я ушла, когда стало тяжело стоя: I left the school when standing at the blackboard got too hard. I still check other people's exercise books with my eyes first, though I haven't held a red pencil for ages.
exact.повариха в столовой авиационного училища: cook in the canteen of the flight college in Guanghan
exact.Меня взяли в столовую авиационного учили: They took me on in the flight college canteen. The cadets ate as if they'd have to fly tomorrow without lunch, and I soon learnt to give them extra.
exact.Я помнила, кто из курсантов не ест остро: I remembered which cadets didn't eat spicy food, and from the way they ate I could guess who had a flight the next day. I was rarely wrong.
exact.Из столовой училища я ушла на пенсию. Ко: I retired from the college canteen. When a plane goes over, I still wonder whether the one flying it has had his lunch.
exact.Я пошла на прядильную фабрику. Смена был: I went to work at a spinning mill. The shifts were long, the fluff hung in the air, and in the evening I'd shake it out of my hair like snow.
exact.Со временем мне дали несколько машин сра: In time they gave me several machines at once. I heard a broken thread before I saw it.
exact.С фабрики я ушла на пенсию. Нитку я до с: I retired from the mill. I still test a thread for breaking before I put it through the needle, though I haven't sewn anything for ages.
exact.Меня приняли на завод, и вместе с работо: They took me on at the factory, and along with the job I got my own unit, a danwei, as we called it. Everything came from there: wages, a place in the hostel, even cinema tickets.
exact.Я уже сама учила новеньких и ругала их т: By then I was training the new girls myself and telling them off just the way I'd been told off. They took offence, and then came back to ask more.
exact.На пенсию я ушла в пятьдесят, как работн: I retired at fifty, as women workers were meant to then. My pass from the factory gate is still in a box at home, just in case they let me in.
exact.После курсов счетоводов меня посадили в: After a bookkeeping course they sat me down at an abacus in the accounts office. The beads clicked all day, and it felt as if the whole office was counting out loud.
exact.На счётах я считала быстрее, чем начальн: I was quicker on the abacus than the boss was on paper, and he stopped checking my work. I could find a mistake by the sound, honestly.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из бухгалтерии, и счёты: I retired from the accounts office, and they gave me the abacus as a leaving present. I still sometimes check my change from the shop on it.
exact.крановщица на Уханьском металлургическом: crane operator at the Wuhan Iron and Steel works
exact.После курсов меня посадили в кабину кран: After a course they put me in a crane cab at the steelworks. From up there people looked tiny, and at first I was afraid even to sneeze.
exact.Я водила кран так плавно, что мастер ста: I drove the crane so smoothly that the foreman held me up as an example to people who'd worked twice as long. Down below they knew me by the way I moved off.
exact.С комбината я ушла на пенсию. Высоты я с: I retired from the steelworks. I haven't been afraid of heights since, but at first I was afraid of the quiet.
exact.работница солевого завода в Цзыгуне: worker at the salt works in Zigong
exact.Я пошла на солевой завод. Соль была везд: I went to work at the salt works. Salt got everywhere, in my hair, in the seams, on my lips, and for the first week I couldn't tell whether I wanted a drink or a cry.
exact.Меня поставили старшей в смене. По тому,: They made me shift leader. From the way the salt crunched underfoot I could tell whether it had dried properly.
exact.С завода я ушла на пенсию. Суп я до сих: I retired from the salt works. I still salt soup by eye and have never got it wrong, and I've no time to taste it anyway.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в Учане н: When I was very little, an uprising began in Wuchang, and a few months later the emperor abdicated. People told me afterwards that the grown-ups kept getting muddled for a long time about what to call everything now.
exact.Осенью в Учане восстали, а зимой объявил: In the autumn there was an uprising in Wuchang, and in the winter they announced there'd be no more emperor. I didn't understand what that meant, but I remember them arguing at home till late at night.
exact.В октябре в Учане началось восстание, в: In October an uprising began in Wuchang, at the end of December Sun Yat-sen was elected provisional president, and in February the court abdicated. It was strange to wake up in a country with no emperor any more.
exact.Потом многое стали называть по-новому, и: Afterwards a lot of things got new names, and the old people kept getting them muddled for a long time.
exact.Помню не столько события, сколько разгов: I remember the talk more than the events: some were glad, some were afraid, some waited for it all to come back. Nobody really knew what would happen next, and everybody pretended they did.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, началась: When I was very little, the war with Japan began. People told me afterwards that even those who'd been enemies the day before agreed to fight together.
exact.Началась война с Японией, и взрослые ста: The war with Japan began, and the grown-ups started talking more quietly. I remember that even the Kuomintang and the Communists, who'd been enemies, announced they were on the same side now.
exact.Началась война с Японией, и в сентябре Г: The war with Japan began, and in September the Kuomintang and the Communists declared a united front. Everyone understood it would be a long one, but nobody thought it would last eight years.
exact.Наш город тогда оказался под японцами. О: Our town was under the Japanese then. People said little about that time, and always more quietly than about anything else.
exact.Новости с тех пор слушали всей семьёй, и: From then on the whole family listened to the news together, and nobody left till it was over.
exact.Я не стану рассказывать того, чего сама: I won't tell you what I didn't see myself. I'll only say the war dragged on so long that children grew up without remembering peacetime.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, японские: When I was very little, the Japanese troops in China surrendered. People told me afterwards that the grown-ups laughed and cried at the same time that day.
exact.В сентябре японские войска сдались, и во: In September the Japanese troops surrendered, and the eight-year war was over. I remember strangers in the street talking to each other as if they'd known each other for years.
exact.Девятого сентября японские войска в Кита: On the ninth of September the Japanese troops in China formally surrendered, and the eight-year war was over. I didn't believe it straight away, I kept waiting for them to announce something else.
exact.Стали загадывать хоть на месяц вперёд, р: People started making plans at least a month ahead, they hadn't done that before.
exact.Радость была, но усталая. Казалось, что: There was joy, but it was a tired joy. It seemed everything would sort itself out now, and I'm still a little sorry for that hope.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, снова нач: When I was very little, the civil war started again. The grown-ups didn't like talking about it, and I learnt early that it was better not to ask.
exact.Летом гражданская война разгорелась снов: In the summer the civil war flared up again, at full force. I remember the grown-ups going quiet when we children came into the room.
exact.Летом гражданская война возобновилась в: In the summer the civil war resumed at full force, just after the Japanese war had ended. We hardly had time to see any peace.
exact.Многие семьи тогда жили врозь, и писем ж: Many families were living apart then, and people waited longer for letters than for each other.
exact.Я не стану говорить о том, чего не знаю: I won't talk about what I don't know for certain. It drove apart people who'd lived side by side, and a great deal went unsaid for years afterwards.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, провозгла: When I was very little, the People's Republic of China was proclaimed. People told me afterwards that the grown-ups remembered that day down to the hour.
exact.Первого октября провозгласили Китайскую: On the first of October the People's Republic of China was proclaimed. The grown-ups said a new life was beginning, and I expected it to start first thing in the morning.
exact.Первого октября Мао Цзэдун провозгласил: On the first of October Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China. Some were glad, others waited to see what would happen, and I think I was both.
exact.Потом поменялись вывески и слова в газет: Afterwards the signs changed and the words in the newspapers changed, but habits changed more slowly.
exact.Помню, как все сразу стали говорить о бу: I remember how everyone suddenly started talking about the future, and more carefully about the past. People felt different things, and I won't pretend everyone felt the same.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, вышел зак: When I was very little, the marriage law came out. They explained to me afterwards that from then on you could only marry if both of you agreed.
exact.Вышел новый закон о браке: замуж теперь: A new marriage law came out: now you married by consent, not by arrangement, and a woman could ask for a divorce herself. The girls in our courtyard discussed it as if it concerned us tomorrow.
exact.Первого мая вышел закон о браке: только: On the first of May the marriage law came out: only with both people's consent, no arranged matches, no second wives or concubines, and a woman could ask for a divorce herself. You could marry from eighteen now.
exact.Сватать не перестали, но спрашивать неве: Matchmaking didn't stop, but now people asked the bride out loud.
exact.Кто-то из старших ворчал, что так распад: Some of the older people grumbled that families would fall apart, and some were quietly glad. I listened to both and thought my own thoughts.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в деревня: When I was very little, the land in the villages was being divided up. People told me afterwards that the grown-ups remembered those years in different ways and didn't like to.
exact.В деревнях тогда шёл передел земли, её з: The land in the villages was being redistributed then, taken from landlords and well-off peasants and given to others. The grown-ups talked about it a lot, but carefully in front of children.
exact.Летом вышел закон о земельной реформе, и: In the summer the land reform law came out, and within two years the land of landlords and well-off peasants had been redistributed. Many people got a plot of their own for the first time.
exact.О том, у кого сколько земли, с тех пор г: After that people talked about who had how much land more carefully than about the weather.
exact.Это было тяжёлое время, и не для всех од: It was a hard time, and not the same for everyone. I won't retell what I didn't see myself, I'll only say that people remembered it very differently afterwards.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, в деревнях созда: When I was little, people's communes with communal canteens were set up in the villages. People told me afterwards how everyone ate together.
exact.Летом в деревнях кооперативы свели в бол: In the summer the cooperatives in the villages were merged into big people's communes, and communal canteens appeared. I thought it was a holiday every day, until the grown-ups started frowning.
exact.Летом, с началом Большого скачка, коопер: In the summer, as the Great Leap Forward began, the cooperatives were merged into people's communes, several thousand households in each, and communal canteens were opened. It seemed everything would be shared now, even the pots.
exact.Работали и ели теперь по звонку, а печь: Now people worked and ate when the bell rang, and the stove at home was sometimes left cold.
exact.Сначала было шумно и даже весело, все за: At first it was noisy and even cheerful, everyone at one table. And a few years later the accounts started being kept by smaller brigades, and that was a bit closer to people.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, всех записали в: When I was little, everyone was registered in the hukou, as town or village. They explained to me afterwards that a great deal depended on that entry.
exact.Вышло положение о прописке, хукоу: каждо: The household registration rules came out, the hukou: everyone was registered to their own place, as town or village. I didn't understand what this paper was, but I saw how carefully the grown-ups kept it.
exact.Вышло положение о хукоу: каждого приписа: The hukou rules came out: everyone was tied to their own place, to a town or a village, and moving from a village to a town became very hard. A paper I'd never noticed before suddenly mattered more than a lot of things.
exact.О переезде с тех пор говорили не «хочу»,: After that people didn't say "I want to move", they said "will they let us".
exact.Многие семьи потом жили врозь не по свое: Afterwards many families lived apart not by choice but by registration. I never thought then that one line could mean so much for so long.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, были голо: When I was very little, there were the hungry years. The grown-ups hardly ever talked about them, and I learnt not to ask.
exact.Начались голодные годы, и тянулись они д: The hungry years began, and they went on a long time. What I remember most is the grown-ups sharing out the food and saying nothing.
exact.С пятьдесят девятого года начались голод: From fifty-nine the hungry years began, and they lasted until sixty-one. It was worst in the villages, especially in Anhui and Sichuan.
exact.С тех пор у нас не оставляли на тарелке: Since then nobody in our house has left a single grain on the plate, even when there was plenty to eat.
exact.Я не стану об этом много говорить. Скажу: I won't say much about it. I'll only say that everyone remembered those years in their own way afterwards, and few talked about them.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, началась Культур: When I was little, the Cultural Revolution began. The grown-ups said little about that time.
exact.Началась Культурная революция, и учёба в: The Cultural Revolution began, and school didn't go on the way it had before. The grown-ups said little, and only at home.
exact.В мае шестьдесят шестого началась Культу: In May sixty-six the Cultural Revolution began, and it went on for ten years, until the autumn of seventy-six. People said little about those years, and when they did, it was under their breath.
exact.Дома научились подолгу говорить о погоде: At home we learnt to talk about the weather for a long time, even when there was nothing to say about the weather.
exact.Я не стану рассказывать больше, чем могу: I won't tell you more than I can. Those were long years, and everyone in our house had their own.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, объявили курс на: When I was little, they announced the course of reform and opening up. I know that from what people told me.
exact.В конце семьдесят восьмого объявили курс: At the end of seventy-eight they announced the course of reform and opening up. The grown-ups argued about where it would lead.
exact.В декабре семьдесят восьмого на пленуме: In December seventy-eight the plenum announced the policy of reform and opening up. At first it was only words in the newspaper, and nobody knew how seriously to take them.
exact.Потом всё стало меняться так быстро, что: Then everything started changing so fast that I stopped being surprised and just started remembering.
exact.Я тогда не понимала, что это надолго. Ка: I didn't understand then that it was for good. It seemed like just another decision, and it turned out to be about the whole rest of my life, about work, prices and even what we ate.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, ввели политику о: When I was little, the one-child policy was introduced. I know that from what people told me.
exact.Ввели политику одного ребёнка, и взрослы: The one-child policy was introduced, and the grown-ups talked about it a lot and in different ways.
exact.Осенью восьмидесятого официально ввели п: In the autumn of eighty the one-child policy was officially introduced. How strict it was depended on the province, and later in the villages they began allowing a second child if the first was a girl.
exact.Во дворах стало меньше братьев и сестёр,: There were fewer brothers and sisters in the courtyards, and you could even see it in the way children played.
exact.Об этом говорили много, но не всегда всл: People talked about it a lot, but not always out loud. I won't decide for others how it was, I'll only say it touched almost every home that was waiting for children.
